newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania PM's parents knew little of appointment.
newsitem.headline: Romania PM's parents knew little of appointment.

text.p: The parents of Romania's Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea knew next to nothing for a time about his appointment - their television set was broken and no one in their Transylvanian village could fix it.

Reporters from two Bucharest newspapers said they were the first to provide Eugenia and Vasile Ciorbea with details of their only son's good fortune after trekking through valleys in the Apuseni mountain range to the village of Ciorbesti.
No roads lead to Ciorbesti, population 300, and the remote village has no telephones.
"I heard, I don't know, I heard something," Eugenia, tears in her eyes, told the daily Adevarul.
Vasile admitted he had "heard it from cousin Stefan who had been listening to the radio".
Soft-spoken Ciorbea was nominated this week after reformist Emil Constantinescu won presidential elections, completing a rout of ex-Communists in parliament earlier this month.

He entered politics after the fall of communism in December 1989 as a trade union leader, joined the opposition Democratic Convention bloc in 1994 and earlier this year became Mayor of Bucharest, defeating former tennis star Ilie Nastase.
"Victor had a tough life. He had no scholarship or a place in residence, because we were labeled as kulaks," Vasile said, referring to landowners victimised under communist rule.
"What he has to do is very difficult. I wouldn't like people to turn against him. Nobody ever spoke badly of him and he never disappointed anybody."
